ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $C$ is a point on line segment $AB$, and $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of $AC$ and $BC$, respectively. If the ratio of the lengths of line segments $CM$ and $CN$ is $2:1$, and the length of line segment $CN$ is $4\,\text{cm}$, find the length of line segment $AB$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since the ratio of the lengths of segments $CM$ and $CN$ is $2\colon 1$ and $CN=4\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ segment $CM=8\,\text{cm}$.\\
Since $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of $AC$ and $BC$ respectively,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=2CM=16\,\text{cm}$, $BC=2CN=8\,\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=AC+BC=16+8=\boxed{24}\,\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment, with the left endpoint labeled A and the right endpoint labeled B; the marks on the line segment from left to right are A, M, C, N, B in sequence, therefore C is on AB, and the image shows the collinear order A-C-B, M is on AC, and N is on CB. Then reason: It is known that CM:CN = 2:1, and CN = 4 cm, so CM = 2 × 4 = 8 cm. Also because the problem gives that M is the midpoint of AC, AC = 2CM = 16 cm; N is the midpoint of BC, so BC = 2CN = 8 cm. From the figure, C is between A and B, AB = AC + BC = 16 + 8 = 24 cm.
